'''Bennedict Richard Felder Mathurin''' (born June 19, 2002) is a Canadian basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. He was named a consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] after his sophomore season.

==Early life and career==
Mathurin is a native of [[Montreal|Montreal, Quebec]] and grew up playing [[ice hockey]] and [[Canadian football|football]] as a [[quarterback]].<ref name="pascoe">{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=With late brother as both memory and motivation, Arizona Wildcats commit Bennedict Mathurin charts course for basketball future |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/with-late-brother-as-both-memory-and-motivation-arizona-wildcats-commit-bennedict-mathurin-charts-course/article_4c38dbe1-5451-5ce8-a465-1555ca04ec4f.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=April 26, 2020}}</ref> He competed for the Quebec provincial basketball team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rose |first1=Aaron |title=Mathurin, Prosper pioneers at NBA Academy |url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/canada-basketball/bennedict-mathurin-olivier-prosper-pioneers-at-nba-academy |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=April 29, 2020}}</ref> In 2018, Mathurin joined the NBA Academy Latin America in [[Mexico City]], becoming its first Canadian-born player.<ref name="holmes">{{cite web |last1=Holmes |first1=C. J. |title=The evolution of Ben Mathurin, and an inside look at the NBA academies |url=https://theathletic.com/1767862/2020/05/04/the-evolution-of-ben-mathurin-and-an-inside-look-at-the-nba-academies/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=May 3, 2020}}</ref> He committed to playing college basketball for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], choosing the Wildcats over [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Arizona Wildcats basketball lands commitment from Ben Mathurin |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2020/01/16/arizona-wildcats-basketball-lands-commitment-ben-mathurin/4487497002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2020}}</ref> He was considered the best Canadian prospect in his class by North Pole Hoops.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sbiet |first1=Elias |title=Bennedict Mathurin Commits to Arizona, Canadian NBA Prospect For The Wildcats |url=https://northpolehoops.com/2020/01/16/bennedict-mathurin-commits-to-arizona-canadian-nba-prospect-for-the-wildcats/ |website=North Pole Hoops |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
On January 2, 2021, Mathurin posted 24 points and 11 rebounds in an 86–82 win over [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kelapire |first1=Ryan |title=Freshman Bennedict Mathurin quickly becoming a star at Arizona |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2021/1/15/22232338/bennedict-mathurin-star-arizona-wildcats-basketball-nba-draft-freshman-oregon-state-wahsington |website=Arizona Desert Swarm |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 15, 2021}}</ref> On January 14, he recorded 31 points and eight rebounds in a 98–64 win over [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Arizona's Bennedict Mathurin is developing into a 'special player,' and more attention is coming |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/arizonas-bennedict-mathurin-is-developing-into-a-special-player-and-more-attention-is-coming/article_7989d03e-cff8-5201-81f3-5818e62dc087.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2021}}</ref> Mathurin averaged 10.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game, shooting 41.8 percent from three-point range. Despite gaining interest as a draft prospect, he decided to return for his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pedersen |first1=Brian |title=Arizona wing Bennedict Mathurin to return for sophomore season |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2021/4/23/22400507/arizona-wildcats-bennedict-mathurin-nba-draft-return-sophomore-tommy-lloyd-2021-wing |website=Arizona Desert Swarm |access-date=April 26, 2021 |date=April 23, 2021}}</ref> On December 11, 2021, Mathurin scored 30 points in a 83-79 win against [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Wildcats G Bennedict Mathurin drops 30 points in Arizona’s win at Illinois |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2932098/wildcats-bennedict-mathurin-drops-30-points-in-arizona-win-at-illinois/ |access-date=January 28, 2022 |work=Arizona Sports |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 11, 2021}}</ref> He was named [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]].<ref name=P12Awards>{{cite press release|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2022/03/08/2021-22-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance|title=2021-22 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}}</ref> 

On April 14, 2022, Mathurin declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-14 |title=Projected lottery pick Bennedict Mathurin declares for NBA draft |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/04/14/arizona-bennedict-mathurin-nba-draft/ |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=The Rookie Wire}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona top prospect Mathurin enters NBA Draft |url=https://theathletic.com/news/bennedict-mathurin-nba-draft/NrYQ9LiyImEO/ |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=The Athletic}}</ref>

==National team career==
Mathurin played for [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Canada]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Riga]] and [[Daugavpils]], Latvia after being cut from the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Olympic team]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Arizona's Bennedict Mathurin dropped from Canada's senior team, expected to join U19 event |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizonas-bennedict-mathurin-dropped-from-canadas-senior-team-expected-to-join-u19-event/article_a4c50af0-d834-11eb-86be-1bdf55995309.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=July 5, 2021 |date=June 28, 2021}}</ref> On July 4, 2021, he scored a team-high 30 points, shooting 11-of-15 from the field and 6-of-9 from three point range, in a 100–75 group stage win over [[Japan men's national under-19 basketball team|Japan]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Amacher |first=Ezra |title=Bennedict Mathurin scores 30 points to lead Canada to win at FIBA U19 World Cup |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2021/7/4/22563068/bennedict-mathurin-30-points-canada-fiba-u19-world-cup-japan-highlights-arizona-wildcats |website=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=July 5, 2021 |date=July 4, 2021}}</ref> One week later, Mathurin scored 31 points to lead Canada to a 101–92 victory over [[Serbia men's national under-19 basketball team|Serbia]] in the third-place game and win the bronze medal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Arizona's Bennedict Mathurin drops 31 points to lead Canada over Serbia for U19 bronze |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizonas-bennedict-mathurin-drops-31-points-to-lead-canada-over-serbia-for-u19-bronze/article_a19cf302-e265-11eb-98ce-6b87e44f9119.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=July 11, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}}</ref> He averaged 16.1 points and four rebounds per game in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bennedict Richard Felder Mathurin (CAN)'s profile – FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2021 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/player/Bennedict-Richard-Felder-Mathurin |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=July 11, 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mathurin is of Haitian descent.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Haitian-Canadian wing Ben Mathurin to pick either Arizona or Baylor on Wednesday |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/haitian-canadian-wing-ben-mathurin-to-pick-either-arizona-or-baylor-on-wednesday/article_98a978dc-3763-11ea-8c08-57a768b44b99.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=January 22, 2021 |date=January 15, 2020}}</ref> His older sister, Jennifer, played college basketball for [[NC State Wolfpack women's basketball|NC State]].<ref name=holmes/> When Mathurin was 12 years old, his 15-year-old brother died in a bicycle accident. He speaks [[English language|English]], [[French language|French]] and [[Haitian Creole|Creole]].<ref name=pascoe/>
